claims.text: The Ingress API is frozen: it stays generally available, the Kubernetes project has no plans to remove it, it gets no further changes, and the project recommends Gateway API instead of Ingress.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking > Ingress (note at top: 'The Ingress API has been frozen'); refs ingress.md lines 24-34

claims.text: Gateway API is an add-on of API kinds defined as custom resources, not natively implemented by Kubernetes; it is the successor to Ingress and must be installed into the cluster.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking > Gateway API (overview; Migrating from Ingress; What's next); refs/kubernetes-website .../gateway.md lines 12-15, 261, 270-274

claims.text: traefik-install.sh applies standard-install.yaml (bundle-version v1.6.2) before Traefik's chart, adding gatewayclasses, gateways, httproutes and other kinds. Traefik's install guide has the reader apply these kinds as a separate step before Traefik.
claims.source_hint: don-hang scripts/k8s/traefik-install.sh L12-17 @stage-3; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/traefik-install.txt L1-13; Traefik docs: Getting Started > Kubernetes ('Install the Gateway API CRDs')

claims.text: apps/traefik.yaml sets providers.kubernetesGateway.enabled: true, so Traefik routes by Gateway API objects as well as by Ingress objects; after the chart installs, GatewayClass traefik exists with controller traefik.io/gateway-controller, ACCEPTED True, beside IngressClass traefik.
claims.source_hint: Traefik docs: Providers > Kubernetes Gateway API; Helm chart values (gatewayClass.enabled); examples/don-hang apps/traefik.yaml lines 21-24; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/traefik-install.txt lines 25-29

claims.text: A GatewayClass contains the name of the controller that implements the class; a Gateway references exactly one GatewayClass by gatewayClassName and is managed by that class's controller.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Gateway API > Resource model; GatewayClass (controllerName); gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io API reference: GatewayClass, Gateway.spec.gatewayClassName

claims.text: A Gateway listener has a name, a port, a protocol and an optional hostname; when hostname is unspecified, the listener matches all hostnames.
claims.source_hint: gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io API reference: Listener (name, hostname, port, protocol; 'When unspecified, all hostnames are matched')

claims.text: An HTTPRoute attaches to a Gateway through spec.parentRefs (name of the Gateway); sectionName selects one listener of that Gateway by its name.
claims.source_hint: gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io API reference: ParentReference (name, sectionName: 'the name of a section within the target resource… Listener name')

claims.text: Gateway API kinds are modeled on roles: a cluster operator owns shared infrastructure such as Gateways, while application developers handle routes for their own Services; a role model, not a rule forbidding teams to edit a Gateway.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Gateway API > Design principles (Role-oriented); gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io: Concepts > Roles and personas

claims.text: In an HTTPRoute, a request must match one of spec.hostnames (compared with the Host header); within a rule, the request matches if any one of the listed matches is satisfied; PathPrefix matches by path prefix.
claims.source_hint: gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io API reference: HTTPRouteSpec.hostnames; HTTPRouteRule.matches ('A request is matched if any of the HTTPRouteMatches match'); PathMatchType PathPrefix

claims.text: HTTPRoute matches can include header matching, and backendRefs carry a weight to split traffic between backends; with Ingress these depend on custom annotations of each controller.

claims.text: An HTTPRoute whose parentRefs names a Gateway that does not exist is still stored by the API server; no controller accepts it, so it has no Accepted=True condition and its paths are not routed.

claims.text: With Traefik, a Gateway listener's port must match the port of a configured Traefik EntryPoint (a mismatch logs an error and is reported in status); 8000 is the port of Traefik's HTTP EntryPoint, so listener http is served there.
